key_insight: A mixed energy estimator combines quantum-prepared states with sparse multiconfiguration references to reduce sampling costs for correlated chemical energy differences.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make quantum simulations of photodynamic materials more practical by reducing measurement demand and tolerating simpler target-state preparation.
method: Combine a quantum-prepared target with sparse multiconfiguration reference states.
Recover ground-state corrections using magnitude-only compute-uncompute measurements.
Validate with emulation and trapped-ion experiments, including AI-assisted state preparation and error detection.
evidence_signal: Analytical variance estimates predict 1.6 mHa precision with a few hundred shots—about 100× fewer than the single-determinant formulation and 1,000× fewer than optimized Hamiltonian-term sampling—while experiments validate the approach up to a (10,10) active space and include a 50-qubit circuit.
watch_item: The headline shot reductions are analytical predictions; performance at larger scales will depend on reference quality, state-preparation costs, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Measurement-efficient energy estimator for quantum chemistry of photodynamic materials
